title: Excellence ascends along weakly etale maps of Noetherian rings
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings, let $f:R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism, assume $R$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], and assume $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. If $f$ is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], meaning that both $R\to S$ and the multiplication homomorphism $S\otimes_R S\to S$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $S$ is excellent.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(iv), printed pp. 146–147 (PDF pages 8–9); Foreword, printed p. 139 (PDF page 1), assumes all rings commutative and Noetherian. Remark 5.2, printed p. 146 (PDF page 8), identifies AF with flatness of R→S and S⊗_R S→S, the definition of weakly etale in Stacks Tag 092B (definition-weakly-etale). Full PDF and extracted text verified in the permitted sandbox; the delivery report records reproducible retrieval, SHA256 and the exact hypothesis comparison. No file in the shared literature tree is claimed to exist.

proof.text: Unfold excellence using [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The hypothesis on $R$ supplies Noetherianity, the G-ring property, J-2, and universal catenarity; in particular $R$ is quasi-excellent. The given Noetherianity of $S$ and weak etaleness of $f$ will be used unchanged in each ascent lemma below. No finite-presentation or faithful-flatness assumption is imposed.

Apply [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] to the quasi-excellent ring $R$ from step 1. It gives that $R$ is Nagata. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization] then says directly that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Nagata. Thus $R$ satisfies both the global Nagata hypothesis of the J-2 ascent lemma and the local Nagata hypothesis of the catenarity ascent lemma.

Use [lem-exc-weakly-etale-g-ring] with $A=R$, $B=S$ and the given $f$. Its source G-ring hypothesis is step 1; its two Noetherian hypotheses are step 1 and the hypothesis on $S$; weak etaleness is the hypothesis on $f$. Its conclusion is that $S$ is a G-ring.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(i), specialization P = geometrically regular; Remark 5.2

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-weakly-etale-nagata-j2] with the same rings and map. Step 2 supplies Nagata for $R$ and step 1 supplies J-2. Both rings are Noetherian and $f$ is weakly etale as checked in step 3. The lemma concludes that $S$ is Nagata and J-2; retain its J-2 conclusion.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-weakly-etale-locally-nagata-catenary]. Step 2 supplies that every prime localization of $R$ is Nagata; step 1 supplies universal catenarity of $R$. The same Noetherian and weakly-etale hypotheses still hold. Its conclusion gives universal catenarity of $S$. The additional conclusion about prime localizations of $S$ is not needed.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190

proof.text: The target $S$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, a G-ring by step 3, J-2 by step 4, and universally catenary by step 5. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] the first three properties make $S$ quasi-excellent, and adjoining universal catenarity makes it excellent. This proves exactly the item, including the zero-ring case where the conditions on prime ideals are vacuous.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(iv), opening proof sentence on printed p. 147; definition 07QT
